title: Upload kept on the host
description: ATTACH-1: the reply to `POST /v1/uploads[?name=<file name>&target=agent|herdr&session=&pane=]` with the file as the raw body (or `multipart/form-data`, one file part plus the same fields). Native and web credentials. The file is kept in `~/.local/state/omodachi/uploads/` (directory 0700, file 0600) as `<agent|herdr|file>-<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<id>.<ext>` for seven days, then swept (at start and hourly). Accepted: images by their signature bytes (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP; HEIC is converted to JPEG on the host, because codex 0.154 silently drops a HEIC image input); PDF by `%PDF-`; text and code by extension, refused if any byte is NUL or another control byte (tab, line breaks and ESC are fine) or the bytes are not UTF-8. The cap is 25 MB (26,214,400 bytes), enforced while the body streams. Refusals are `http-error` documents: `413 upload_too_large`, `415 upload_svg_refused` (SVG is script-bearing markup), `415 upload_type_refused` (anything not listed - a `.zip`, an AVIF), `415 upload_not_text` (a text name over binary or non-UTF-8 bytes), `415 upload_heic_unconvertible`, `400 upload_empty`. `id` is what a send carries in `attachments`; `path` is absolute on the host and is what a Herdr pane receives in place of the chip's marker; `name` is the sanitised name the phone sent (a converted HEIC is named `.jpg`), shown on the chip only. `DELETE /v1/uploads/{id}` removes it before a send (`upload-removed.schema.json`).
